title: Tracing absorption information in terahertz discrimination of medicinal materials
article_type: Submitted Papers / original research; match the portal option
abstract: Terahertz screening of medicinal materials benefits from identifying which spectral information supports a prediction and how additional labelled specimens change it. We investigated paired absorption and refractive-index spectra from 1,672 specimens representing four investigator-labelled materials. A common absorption classifier correctly classified 174/174 Suanzaoren–Zaoren prediction specimens and 331/339 specimens across all four materials. Representation analysis used 300 Suanzaoren specimens from five balanced source groups with repeated nested cross-validation. Monte Carlo partial-least-squares coefficient ranking followed by support vector classification achieved 93.44% mean accuracy with internally selected absorption features. At a fixed budget of 62 predictors, selection from a joint SNV absorption–refractive-index pool achieved 87.11%, compared with 81.00% for SNV absorption-only selection. All 930 retained feature occurrences across the 15 joint-pool refits were nevertheless absorption coordinates, revealing a candidate-pool effect on the selected absorption subsets. Separate support-set controls showed that adding valid labels increased five-source accuracy from 80.00% to 83.78% while retaining source-fitted standardization and kernel scale; unlabelled-statistics and loss-mass controls identified effective supervision as the principal explanation. Two accepted isolated-molecule calculations for protocatechuic acid provided 45 positive vibrational modes and independent infrared intensities, with lowest frequencies above the experimental modelling window. Together, these results connect medicinal-material discrimination to the variables and supervision actually used, supporting compact terahertz fingerprints with explicitly defined spectral and molecular interpretation.
